École Laurier is a francophone public elementary school of the Centre de services scolaire de
Montréal (CSSDM) in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal. This report describes it in three layers: the school
itself, the kilometre around it, and what a three-bedroom home there costs to buy or rent this
month. It is the first output of MTL-101's `school-report` skill, run as a dry run, and the
school was picked because it is not a simple case: its pupils have spent four school years in a
temporary building three kilometres away in Villeray, so the report shows both kilometres.

::: {.callout-important}
## Not a ranking

Each zone metric is shown with its decile among the 229 francophone public elementary schools on
the island outside the West Island, marked [d1]{.decile-low} to [d3]{.decile-low} for the lowest
three tenths, [d4]{.decile-mid} to [d7]{.decile-mid} for the middle, and [d8]{.decile-high} to
[d10]{.decile-high} for the top three. A high decile means a high value, nothing
more, so the label says which way is favourable for a family: ▲ higher is favourable (children,
parks, stations), ▼ lower is favourable (crime, collisions, deprivation, cost), and rows with no
glyph are descriptive. On the ▲ and ▼ rows the most favourable of the compared zones is [shaded]{.best}.
The report computes no composite score, and the IMSE is a socioeconomic index of the pupils enrolled,
not a measure of academic performance.
:::

# The school

::: {.callout-important}
## Relocated to Villeray since 2022, return announced for the 2026-2027 rentrée

The home building at 505 avenue Laurier Est has been under a $28M renovation (façades and
masonry, interior finishes, a new ventilation system, a rebuilt daycare space and library)
since 2022, and the school community has been housed at 7378 rue Lajeunesse in Villeray,
about 3 km north.[^cssdm-laurier] The move was planned for two school years and was extended
twice; in May 2025 parents learned the pupils would not return for 2025-2026 either.[^mp-2025]
In December 2025 the school's governing board wrote 505 avenue Laurier Est into the 2026-2027
establishment act with 85% of interior work complete, the principal warning that a project of
this size "always involves its share of unforeseen circumstances".[^mp-dec] The school's own
news page reports that the CSSDM board confirmed the return at its meeting of 18 February
2026, subject to the remaining works; that page could not be opened directly and the fact is
*unverified* here.[^retour] The tables below therefore show two zones for Laurier: the Plateau
kilometre a family would live in once the school is back, and the Villeray kilometre pupils
commute to today.
:::

| | |
|:---|:---|
| Service centre | Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (762000) |
| MEQ code | 762103 |
| Home building | Laurier, 505 avenue Laurier Est, H2J 1E9 (préscolaire and primaire) |
| Temporary building | 7378 rue Lajeunesse, H2R 2H8, Villeray (since 2022) |
| Program | Regular program of a neighbourhood school; the school describes an approach built on youth literature, music, visual arts and sport (*unverified*: school site returned 403, wording from its indexed pages)[^prog] |
| Admission | Neighbourhood school, by address; registration files are currently received at the temporary building (*unverified*, same source)[^prog] |
| Pupils (2025-2026) | 278 in the MEQ index file; the CSSDM project page describes a school of about 530 pupils, which reads as the renovated building's capacity[^cssdm-laurier] |
| IMSE 2025-2026 | 3.24, decile 2 |
| SFR 2025-2026 | 5.62, decile 7 |
| Website | <https://laurier.cssdm.gouv.qc.ca/> |

: The school in one table; facts marked *unverified* could not be confirmed on a page that loaded {#tbl-school}

The MEQ's IMSE places the school in decile 2 for 2025-2026 (1 = most advantaged, 10 = most
disadvantaged; 8 to 10 is the official *milieu défavorisé*). It is built from the enrolled
pupils' parents' education and employment, not from test results. Here it agrees with the
census picture of the Plateau kilometre in @tbl-people, where the no-diploma share is in the
lowest decile and household income in the eighth; the SFR, which tracks low-income families,
sits higher at decile 7, and the zone's low-income rate is likewise near the island median.
The 278 pupils are counted in Villeray, where they currently attend, but their addresses are
still the Plateau's.

[^mp-2025]: [Les travaux à l'école Laurier s'étirent encore une fois](https://www.monplateau.info/le-retour-des-eleves-a-lecole-laurier-est-reporte-de-nouveau/), monplateau.info, 15 May 2025.
[^mp-dec]: [L'école Laurier pourrait rouvrir dans Le Plateau à la rentrée 2026-2027](https://www.monplateau.info/lecole-laurier-pourrait-rouvrir-dans-le-plateau-a-la-rentree-2026-2027/), monplateau.info, 22 December 2025.
[^retour]: [Retour de la communauté scolaire à l'école Laurier dès la rentrée 2026-2027](https://laurier.cssdm.gouv.qc.ca/nouvelles/travaux/retour-de-la-communaute-scolaire-a-lecole-laurier-des-la-rentree-2026-2027/), École Laurier; the site returns HTTP 403 to automated requests, so the content is quoted from its search-index extract.
[^prog]: [École primaire Laurier](https://laurier.cssdm.gouv.qc.ca/) and its [Notre projet éducatif](https://laurier.cssdm.gouv.qc.ca/ecole/projet-educatif/) page; same 403, same caveat.

# The zone

The zone is a circle of one kilometre around the school building, a stand-in for the catchment
polygon that exists only in the CSSDM's finder and PDF maps. Laurier gets two columns, one per
address. The comparators, chosen by the reader, are the two nearest Plateau neighbourhood
schools, Paul-Bruchési (675 m) and Lanaudière (1.1 km), and École FACE (470 m), the closest
school of all but an arts school with CSSDM-wide lottery admission rather than a neighbourhood
school. The four Plateau circles overlap heavily, which is why their columns move together.

temporary building in Villeray; the grey pins are the comparators; the M squares are métro
stations inside either kilometre.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the table

The four Plateau circles are among the most populous zones on the island and describe the same
population: few children and few households with children (bottom two deciles), high incomes,
almost nobody without a diploma, and more than half the residents arrived within five years,
the most mobile tenth of the island. The Villeray kilometre around the temporary building is
close to the Plateau on income and education, has slightly more children and fewer low-income
residents, and sits a little lower on mobility. On this table the temporary site is not a
different world, only a slightly more settled one.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Social deprivation is high across central Montreal

Nine in ten Plateau residents live in areas the INSPQ ranks socially deprived while almost none
live in materially deprived ones. The social axis counts people living alone and lone-parent
families, which the Plateau is full of; read it with the households-with-children line of
@tbl-people rather than as a warning.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the table

All five zones are in the top three deciles on nearly every line, which is what the central
boroughs look like once incidents are divided by residents: dense, commercial and
visited by people who do not live there. The Plateau circle around Laurier and the one around
Lanaudière are top-decile on the total; the temporary Villeray site is lower on vehicle crime
and the total but not on violence. The pedestrian and cyclist line is the one that concerns a
school run: both Laurier circles are in the top decile, and 500 m from 505 Laurier Est takes in
avenue Laurier Est around métro Laurier, while the Villeray site sits on rue Lajeunesse
between rue Jean-Talon and rue Jarry.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## What these two datasets cannot say

The city states the incident file is not official SPVM statistics; positions are moved to the
nearest intersection and 17% of incidents have no coordinates and are absent from the rates.
The collision extract ends in 2021; its last two years are pandemic years. Both are rates of
reported events, not of risk.
:::

with a quarter of its dwellings condominiums, in the top two deciles, and a third in plexes. The
Villeray kilometre is more of a plex belt, half its dwellings in two- to five-unit buildings,
and is assessed lower on every type, by about a sixth for houses and plexes and by less for

disguise.

The Plateau circle around Laurier holds less park per resident than the island median, in the
third decile: parc Sir-Wilfrid-Laurier lies inside it, but parc La Fontaine begins about two
hundred metres beyond its southern edge. The Lanaudière circle, 1.1 km east, contains the whole
of parc La Fontaine and is top-decile on park share. Almost half of parc Jarry falls inside the
Villeray circle. On transit the two Laurier addresses are the best served of the five: métro
Laurier's entrance is across the street from the home building, and the temporary site is a
few minutes' walk from Jean-Talon and De Castelnau, each kilometre holding three stations of
the orange line.

# Sources and caveats

- **School facts**: the CSSDM project page and two monplateau.info articles were opened on
  2026-09-18; the school's own pages return HTTP 403 to automated requests, so its program
  description, its admission wording and the 18 February 2026 board confirmation are quoted
  from search-index extracts and marked *unverified*.
- **IMSE/SFR**: MEQ, *Indices de défavorisation*, Données Québec, school year 2025-2026.
- **Zone tables**: `scripts/zone_stats.py` on open data fetched on 2026-09-18 (Ville de
  Montréal, Données Québec, INSPQ, Statistics Canada 2021 Census; métro and REM stations from
  OpenStreetMap contributors). Dissemination areas by
  centroid: 64 for the Plateau circle, 72 for the Villeray circle, 66, 72 and 70 for the
  comparators; the city's equity index covers all residents of every zone; tax bills matched
  99.9% of assessment units. Census 2021 is five years old; assessed values are from the
  2026-2028 roll and reflect the July 2024 market.
- **Listings**: as seen on Centris.ca on 2026-09-18, see the source column of each table.
- **Deciles**: among 229 in-scope schools, from `data/derived/zone_stats_all.parquet`;
  reproduced by the commands in the Scripts section of the repository's CLAUDE.md.

# Conclusion

Four readings, in the order a parent weighs them. Each states what the tables show, not a
verdict.

**School.** A regular-program neighbourhood school of the CSSDM whose pupils sit in IMSE
decile 2, the second most advantaged tenth of Quebec's schools, with the SFR at decile 7 the
one line pointing the other way. Its building has been under renovation since 2022 and the
pupils are three kilometres away in Villeray; the return to 505 avenue Laurier Est is announced
for the 2026-2027 rentrée, subject to the remaining works (@tbl-school).

**Safety.** Both Laurier kilometres are in the top deciles on every crime category, as are the
three comparators: dense central boroughs divided by their resident count look like this. The
line that concerns a school run is the pedestrian and cyclist victims within 500 m, top decile
for both Laurier addresses and for Lanaudière, seventh for Paul-Bruchési (@tbl-safety). Both
datasets are rates of reported events, one obfuscated and one ending in 2021.

**Livability.** The Plateau kilometre has few children and few households with children
(bottom deciles), almost no adults without a diploma, and the island's most mobile population;
the Villeray kilometre is slightly more settled and reads like the Plateau on education and
income. Materially deprived areas are rare in both, socially deprived ones common, which is the
household mix of the centre rather than a warning. Park space per resident is below the island
median around 505 Laurier Est, with parc La Fontaine just beyond the circle; métro Laurier is
at the door, and three orange-line stations fall inside each Laurier kilometre (@tbl-people,
@tbl-indices, @tbl-parks).

**Affordability.** Old stock, a quarter condominiums; assessed values and tax bills in the top
two deciles on every type for the Plateau and slightly lower for Villeray, at the island's
effective tax rate. This month's three-bedroom listings start around half a million dollars to
buy and in the low two thousands a month to rent, with a Plateau triplex above a million
(@tbl-stock, @tbl-cost, @tbl-for-sale, @tbl-for-rent).

Next steps for this school:

1. **Confirm the catchment** for the family's candidate addresses on the CSSDM finder; the
   circle is a stand-in, and the Plateau's neighbourhood schools sit within a kilometre of each
   other.
2. **Watch the return.** The 2026-2027 rentrée at 505 avenue Laurier Est is announced subject
   to the remaining works; a family enrolling for 2026-2027 should ask the school which
   building the year starts in.
3. **Registration calendar.** The CSSDM's registration window for a neighbourhood school runs
   each January (7 to 27 January 2026 for the 2026-2027 year), by appointment at the school,
   with two proofs of address and the birth certificate; Laurier's files are received at the
   temporary building while the relocation lasts.[^inscr]
4. **What this report does not yet cover**: childcare places, transit frequency, heat islands,
   rents by CMHC zone, and the secondary school the zone feeds.

[^inscr]: [Étapes, conditions et formulaires : inscription dans les écoles](https://www.cssdm.gouv.qc.ca/admission-inscription/procedure-inscription/), CSSDM, read through its search-index extract on 2026-09-18.

::: {.callout-important}
## Bottom line

École Laurier is a neighbourhood school whose pupils and kilometre are among the most
advantaged on the island by education and income, in a zone that is dense, old, expensive and
busy on the street. The one fact to verify before acting is which building the school opens
in for 2026-2027.
:::
